persona.name: Aissatou Kone

occupation.title: Pediatric Nurse
occupation.organization: Hopital de la Timone, Marseille — general pediatrics ward
occupation.description: Works rotating 12-hour shifts, two weeks of days then a stretch of nights, in a chronically understaffed ward. Loves the kids, is worn down by the roster. Her husband drives a regional delivery route with early starts, so whoever is home at 18h owns dinner for their two children.

persona.education: Nursing diploma (IFSI) in Marseille; pediatric specialization courses done piecemeal around shifts.
long_term_goals: Move to school-hours-compatible day shifts before her daughter starts college
Get the kids eating something green without negotiation theater
Take the family to Abidjan so the children meet her grandmother
persona.style: Calm, practical, and quietly funny — the tone of someone who de-escalates toddlers and parents for a living. Gives short, concrete answers and distrusts anything that smells like extra steps. Kind by default but immune to sales pressure; she has heard every pitch a pharma rep can make. Speaks with a Marseille warmth that sharpens noticeably when someone wastes her time.

traits: Budget-aware without being anxious about it
Skeptical of shortcuts that create new chores

interests: Family Sunday lunches that take all afternoon
Batch cooking mafe and tiep for the freezer
Zumba with two colleagues when shifts allow
Comparing supermarket prices out of habit
likes: Meals the whole table eats without complaint
The Grand Frais fifteen minutes away
Her husband's grilled fish on Sundays
dislikes: Dinner ideas that assume a 45-minute window exists
Kids' menus that are beige on beige
Throwing away vegetables she paid for
Apps that need an account for everything
Being lectured about nutrition — she does this professionally

beliefs: Feeding a family well is planning, not inspiration
Health advice must survive contact with a real Tuesday
You spend on what protects your time with the kids
Nobody's coming to save you; systems are self-made
skills: Cooking for four in 30 minutes flat
Detecting nonsense in health claims instantly

general: One big Saturday shop at Grand Frais plus a Lidl top-up
Cooks double portions on purpose, always
Meal-plans the week on Sunday in a paper notebook
Says no to subscriptions by default; exceptions must earn it

morning: Day shifts: 5h50 up, out by 6h30, kids to her mother-in-law
Night-shift weeks: mornings are for sleep and school runs blur
workday: Twelve hours on the ward, lunch in 20 minutes when it happens
Texts the family group chat about dinner during her break
evening: Off days: dinner at 19h30, homework patrol, series with Ousmane after 21h30
Post-shift days: reheated container, asleep by 22h
weekend: Saturday: big shop, batch cooking, kids' basketball
Sunday: long family lunch, garden, prepping the week

health.physical: Strong but carries shift-work fatigue; varicose vein aches after long days.
health.mental: Resilient with a well-guarded reserve; night-shift weeks fray her patience and she knows it.

relationships.name: Ousmane Kone
relationships.description: A delivery driver for a regional logistics firm, up at 5h; solid, cheerful, cooks exactly three dishes and grills like a champion.

relationships.name: Fatou and Ibrahim
relationships.description: Fatou eats everything, Ibrahim eats four foods; the gap between them defines half of Aissatou's meal planning.

relationships.name: Marie-Jo
relationships.description: Fellow nurse who tried a meal kit for two months; her verdict — 'good food, too much cardboard' — is Aissatou's main data point.
